title: 2014 HMMT February Guts Problem 3
statement: Let \(A B C D E F\) be a regular hexagon. Let \(P\) be the circle inscribed in \(\triangle B D F\). Find the ratio of the area of circle \(P\) to the area of rectangle \(A B D E\).

solutions.text: \(\quad \frac{\pi \sqrt{3}}{12}\) Let the side length of the hexagon be \(s\). The length of \(B D\) is \(s \sqrt{3}\), so the area of rectangle \(A B D E\) is \(s^{2} \sqrt{3}\). Equilateral triangle \(B D F\) has side length \(s \sqrt{3}\). The inradius of an equilateral triangle is \(\sqrt{3} / 6\) times the length of its side, and so has length \(\frac{s}{2}\). Thus, the area of circle \(P\) is \(\frac{\pi s^{2}}{4}\), so the ratio is \(\frac{\pi s^{2} / 4}{s^{2} \sqrt{3}}=\frac{\pi \sqrt{3}}{12}\).
